items.question: What attainment makes a practitioner dear to the yoginīs?
premises: Enjoyment and liberation constitute a great accomplishment
Such accomplishment belongs to the practitioner
This accomplishment inspires affection in the yoginīs
items.inference: A practitioner possessing the great accomplishment of enjoyment and liberation becomes dear to the yoginīs.
items.plain_english: He may become dear to the yoginīs, possessing the great accomplishment of enjoyment and liberation.

rows.grounds: first member of place name compound
second member of place name compound

items.question: Which chapter concludes after emerging in Candra-dvīpa?
premises: A chapter is identified by ordinal number
This chapter is the ninth
It emerged in Candra-dvīpa
items.inference: The ninth chapter, which emerged in Candra-dvīpa, is concluded.
items.plain_english: Thus ends the ninth chapter, which emerged in Candra-dvīpa.

items.question: How should the practitioner visualize the self surrounded by fire?
premises: The self is surrounded by fire
The self is positioned in a specific posture
The posture involves standing on one foot
items.inference: The practitioner should visualize the self surrounded by fire and standing on one foot.
items.plain_english: Visualize the self surrounded by fire, standing on one foot.

items.question: What request does the goddess make regarding the determination of knowledge?
premises: The goddess addresses the god
She seeks the determination of knowledge
She asks for it to be made manifest now
items.inference: The goddess requests that the determination of knowledge be made manifest to her now.
items.plain_english: O God, make manifest to me now the determination of knowledge.

items.question: What division of the eight octads does the goddess seek to know fully?
premises: There is a division of eight octads
The goddess desires complete knowledge of it
She seeks to know it in its endless extent
items.inference: The goddess seeks to know fully and endlessly the division of the eight octads.
items.plain_english: And I wish to know fully and endlessly the division of the eight octads.

items.question: How can the secret place and wheel be quickly accomplished according to the goddess?
premises: The goddess asks about a secret place
She asks about the wheel
She seeks the means for quick accomplishment
items.inference: The goddess asks Bhairava how the secret place and the wheel are quickly accomplished.
items.plain_english: O Bhairava, tell me how the secret place and the wheel are quickly accomplished.

items.question: How does Bhairava respond to the goddess's request for rare knowledge?
premises: Bhairava expresses approval
He acknowledges being asked by the goddess
The requested knowledge is hard for gods to obtain
items.inference: Bhairava approves and states that the goddess has asked about something hard for even the gods to obtain.
items.plain_english: Well said, well said, O great goddess! You have asked me about something hard for even the gods to obtain.

items.question: Which bodily locations correspond to the syllables kṣa and laṃ?
premises: The syllable kṣa is identified with the brahmarandhra
The syllable laṃ is assigned a bodily location
That location is the forehead
items.inference: The syllable kṣa corresponds to the brahmarandhra, and the syllable laṃ corresponds to the forehead.
uncertainties: lalāṭayoḥ is dual in form though often used for the forehead region
items.plain_english: The syllable kṣa is the brahmarandhra, and the syllable laṃ is in the forehead.

items.question: Which bodily locations correspond to the syllables ṣa and śa?
premises: The syllable ṣa is assigned to the throat region
The syllable śa is assigned to the heart
These placements are stated in sequence
items.inference: The syllable ṣa corresponds to the throat region, and the syllable śa corresponds to the heart.
items.plain_english: The syllable ṣa is in the throat region, and the syllable śa is then in the heart.

items.question: What instruction follows the declaration of the place-wheels?
premises: The place-wheels have been declared
These wheels have an associated meditation
The beloved is commanded to listen
items.inference: After declaring the place-wheels, Bhairava instructs the beloved to hear their meditation.
items.plain_english: Thus the place-wheels have been declared; now hear their meditation, O beloved.

items.question: How is the divine lotus of the first octad described for meditation?
premises: The lotus is divine
It has eight spokes
It is adorned by the first octad
items.inference: The meditation object is a divine eight-spoked lotus adorned by the first octad.
items.plain_english: Visualize a divine eight-spoked lotus adorned by the first octad.

items.question: What conduct should a practitioner with equanimous mind abandon through practice?
premises: Practice leads to an equanimous mind
Certain social duties are contrasted with this state
The practitioner is instructed to abandon village dharma
items.inference: Through practice, one who has attained equanimity of mind should abandon village dharma.
uncertainties: grāma-dharmañ may refer to conventional social or household duties
items.plain_english: Through practice, becoming even-minded, one should abandon the dharma of village life.

items.question: What siddhis arise from the practice described to the beloved?
premises: The practice yields special knowledge
One result is knowledge of distant hearing
Another result is paralysis of bonds
items.inference: The practice grants knowledge of distant hearing and likewise the paralysis of bonds.
uncertainties: pāśa-stobham may mean arresting or immobilizing bonds or enemies
items.plain_english: One gains knowledge of hearing from afar and likewise the power to paralyze bonds, O beloved.

items.question: What further powers are briefly attributed to this practice?
premises: Additional results are being summarized
Immortality is included among them
Transformation is also included
items.inference: In brief, the practice also yields immortality and transformation.
uncertainties: parivartanam could refer to bodily transformation or reversal of conditions
items.plain_english: Likewise, O goddess, in brief, one attains immortality and transformation.

items.question: How is the second eight-petaled lotus characterized in meditation?
premises: A second lotus is introduced
It has eight petals
It is well illuminated by meditation on fire
items.inference: The second eight-petaled lotus is well illuminated through meditation on fire.
items.plain_english: The second is an eight-petaled lotus, well illuminated by meditation on fire.

items.question: What ability arises for one whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation?
premises: The mind becomes absorbed in one-pointed meditation
The practitioner performs an action of making
The result is manifold forms
items.inference: One whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation can assume many forms.
items.plain_english: One whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation can assume many forms.

items.question: What destructive power is attributed to the practitioner when angered?
premises: The practitioner is in a state of anger
The action affects the entire triple world
The triple world includes moving and unmoving beings
items.inference: When angered, the practitioner can destroy the entire triple world with all its moving and unmoving beings.
items.plain_english: When angry, he can destroy the entire triple world, with all that moves and does not move.

items.question: What liberating function is attributed to the third great wheel?
premises: A third great wheel is introduced
It has a liberating function
Its scope includes the nine principles
items.inference: The third great wheel is the liberator from the nine principles.
uncertainties: nava-tattva may refer to a specific set of nine principles in this system
items.plain_english: The third is the great wheel, which liberates one from the nine principles.

items.question: What bodily and perceptual powers result from this wheel's practice?
premises: The practice affects bodily aging signs
Wrinkles and grey hair are destroyed
The practice also grants distant seeing
items.inference: This practice brings the destruction of wrinkles and grey hair and likewise the power of seeing from very far away.
items.plain_english: It brings the destruction of wrinkles and grey hair, and likewise the power to see from very far away.

items.question: What disciplined practice in solitude enables the creation of many forms?
premises: The practice is performed in solitude
The practitioner must be intent on meditation
The practitioner is commanded to create many forms
items.inference: In solitude, intent on meditation, the practitioner should create many forms.
items.plain_english: In solitude, intent on meditation, create many forms.

items.question: What result comes from being devoted to constant practice?
premises: The practitioner is devoted to constant practice
The practice produces a specific attainment
That attainment is immortality
items.inference: One devoted to constant practice indeed attains immortality.
items.plain_english: Indeed, one who is devoted to constant practice attains immortality.

items.question: How does abstaining from food by day affect age and death?
premises: A regimen of non-eating by day is practiced
This practice affects the condition of aging and death
The result is expressed as going beyond death of age
items.inference: By abstaining from food during the day, one will overcome death associated with age.
uncertainties: divasāt nāśanena may mean fasting during the day or gradual reduction by days
items.plain_english: By abstaining from food during the day, one will overcome the death of old age.

items.question: What bodily form results from constant yogic practice over sixteen years?
premises: The practitioner engages in constant yogic practice
The duration indicated is two times eight years
This practice produces a specific bodily form
items.inference: Through constant yogic practice, one attains the form of a sixteen-year-old.
items.plain_english: Through constant yogic practice, one attains the form of a sixteen-year-old.

items.question: What cosmic power arises from contemplating a smoke-colored form?
premises: The practitioner contemplates a smoke-colored form
The contemplation is performed always
This practice affects the triple world
items.inference: By always contemplating a smoke-colored form, one can shake the triple world.
items.plain_english: Always contemplating a smoke-colored form, one can shake the triple world, O beloved.
